data.long_meaning: The name Truman is derived from the English words 'true' and 'man'. It was originally used as a nickname for someone who was considered a true man in character and actions. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Truman usually hope their child will grow to embody true man and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Truman has a notable place in American history as it was borne by Harry S. Truman, the 33rd President of the United States. Truman rose to prominence as President Roosevelt's vice president, and upon Roosevelt's death in 1945, Truman assumed the presidency. He led the country through the end of World War II, the onset of the Cold War, and the beginning of the United States' involvement in the Korean War. The name came to represent steadfastness and leadership.
data.spiritual_significance: Truman can also be seen as a symbol of faithfulness and trustworthiness in the spiritual sense. The name encourages one to be a true man or woman of character, an individual who reflects the virtues of honesty, integrity, and reliability. Truman's name serves as a reminder of the importance of being true to one's beliefs, values, and commitments in life.
